title: Design System: FitPro
note: React Native / Expo (adaptive: iOS + Android) project. No live-mode browser panel applies here, so component entries are omitted rather than fabricating HTML/CSS snippets that would never render against this codebase. Tonal ramps are omitted for the same reason: nothing consumes them.

label.purpose: Uppercase small-caps field labels and chrome, e.g. TextField's label.

caption.purpose: Secondary/supporting copy, e.g. EmptyState message text, list row metadata.

body.purpose: Default readable text: button labels, input text, pill labels, most screen paragraph text.

subtitle.purpose: Emphasis text between body and title, e.g. home's secondary macro numbers (protein/fat/carbs), the brand wordmark.

title.purpose: Screen and section titles across every screen, negative tracking.

display.purpose: One hero numeral per screen that should be unmistakable at a glance, e.g. home's calorie target. Not a general-purpose large-text step.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Default resting shadow for every solid surface (cards, buttons, fields, pills).

shadows.name: button-primary
shadows.purpose: Colored glow under the primary button and selected ChoiceGroup pill.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Press-down feedback on Button and ChoiceGroup pills. Near-instant, no overshoot.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Focus and selection state transitions on TextField and ChoiceGroup. Critically damped, slightly slower settle.

narrative.overview: FitPro's visual system sits at the tension between two things: the warmth of a coach who's rooting for you, and the restraint of Apple-grade native materials. It borrows its material vocabulary from Apple Fitness and Apple Health -- soft ambient shadows at rest, real native glass (Liquid Glass via expo-glass-effect) for floating chrome, spring-based motion that responds to touch instead of playing a fixed animation -- but it never lets that craft read as cold or clinical. The palette is warm off-whites and a single vital red, not slate grays and blue gradients; type never shouts a calorie count at you. The system explicitly rejects the loud gamification of free fitness apps -- streak badges, aggressive notification chrome, flashy stat walls -- and the opposite failure mode of a dense manual-logging tool where every screen is a table to fill in. This app plans for the user; the interface should feel like it's handing you a finished week, not asking you to build one.
keyCharacteristics: One committed accent (vital red) against warm neutrals -- never a full palette of competing colors.
Real native materials (glass, springs) reserved for chrome and moments that earn them, not decoration everywhere.
Numbers (calories, macros, weight) are present but never the loudest thing on any screen.
Every interactive surface responds on press-down, not on release -- the interface feels alive under the finger.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Vital Red is the only saturated color in the system. If a second saturated color feels tempting for a new state (success, warning), reach for weight, motion, or an icon before reaching for a second hue.

rules.name: The Size-Specific Tracking Rule
rules.body: No fixed letterSpacing value is reused across sizes. Tracking goes negative as text grows past body (Subtitle, Title) and positive as it shrinks below body (Caption, Label) -- matching Apple's own optical-sizing discipline rather than applying one tracking value everywhere.

rules.name: The Earned Glass Rule
rules.body: Real glass material is reserved for chrome that genuinely floats over other content (the tab bar) or surfaces that opt in explicitly (Card variant="glass"). It is never the default surface treatment -- most cards, buttons, and fields are flat Pure White with a Card shadow, exactly as before glass was introduced.

dos: Do use Vital Red (#DC2626) as the only saturated color on any screen -- it should always mean "this is the action" or "this is selected."
Do start every press interaction on press-down (onPressIn), never wait for release to show feedback.
Do animate state changes (focus, selection) with the settle spring instead of an instant style swap.
Do fall back to a flat Pure White + Card shadow surface wherever real glass material isn't available -- never ship a half-broken translucent look.
Do respect the OS reduced-motion and reduced-transparency settings on every animated or glass surface.
donts: Don't add a second saturated accent color alongside Vital Red -- reach for weight, motion, or an icon instead.
Don't use streak badges, aggressive push-style in-app banners, or flashy stat walls.
Don't build dense manual-logging tables in the MyFitnessPal mold -- the app plans for the user.
Don't add a border that only appears on focus/selection and shifts layout.
Don't use real glass material as a decorative default on every surface -- it's reserved for floating chrome and explicit opt-in.
